note: Descriptive matter for the nine manas, the months-and-asterisms table of xiv.15-16 and the shadasitimukhas of xiv.4-6. The uses listed for each mana are summarised from the design for this chapter, not copied from verse text; check them against corpus records for SS.14.1-19 before quoting.

uses: The span from creation to dissolution; never used in computation

manas.unit: solar year, one day and night of the gods
uses: One year of men is one day and night of the gods

manas.unit: lunar month, one day and night of the Fathers
uses: The new moon is the Fathers' midday and the full moon their midnight
Fourteen manvantaras with fifteen sandhis make a kalpa

manas.unit: Jovian year, a twelfth of Jupiter's revolution
uses: Names the years of the Jovian cycle from Jupiter's heliacal rising and setting

manas.unit: solar day, one degree of the Sun's motion
uses: The measure of day and night
The auspicious time at a sign entry
The reckoning of civil days and weekdays
The count of days since the epoch
The tithis and the lunar month
Times for rites reckoned by the Moon
The sidereal day and the asterisms

shadasitimukhas.note: Burgess's note to xiv.6 finds no explanation of the division of the Sun's path into arcs of 86 degrees and says the commentary offers nothing on its character. The four longitudes are text; what they are for is not.
shadasitimukhas.remainder_use: Offerings to the Fathers in the last sixteen degrees of Virgo are inexhaustible (v.6).
